newsitem.title: USA: Hispanics equally prone to common U.S. genetic ill.
newsitem.headline: Hispanics equally prone to common U.S. genetic ill.

text.p: The most common genetic disorder in the United States, which causes iron to build up in the body and damage organs, occurs as often among Hispanics as non-Hispanics, federal health experts said on Thursday.
Researchers have long known that hereditary haemochromatosis, the cause of most cases of iron overload disease, mostly affects white males of northern European descent.

But the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said screening of 15,000 patients at a San Diego health maintenance organisation had found that the prevalence of iron overload among Hispanics was similar to that of non-Hispanics.
One in 10 Americans carries the gene that causes iron overload. One in every 200 to 250 has the disease.

People with it accumulate iron in their body over their lifetime. By about the age of 40, the accumulation exceeds the body's ability to store it, and the iron inflames and damages body organs. It can cause arthritis, cirrhosis of the liver, diabetes, impotence, heart failure and death, the CDC said.
